# Milestone results (auto-generated by `python -m markov_rl.report`; facts only)

## 1. Tokenization and chunk size

- Tokenizer: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (digits are single tokens).
- Tokens per trace line incl. newline (N=32 programs): verbose mean 14.5 (min 8, max 17); terse mean 7.7.
- Minimal state size s_min (content `pc=..;a=..;...`, worst case 2-digit pc; tags not counted): k=4: 20, k=8: 40, k=16: 72 tokens (proposal guessed 25/45/85). `<mem></mem>` tags = 5 tokens.
- Prompt tokens (program, empty state), mean: N=8: 107, N=16: 165, N=32: 284, N=64: 519
- Verbose trace tokens (max over 300 programs): N=8: 129, N=16: 255, N=32: 508, N=64: 993

Chunks needed (verbose; full/tail = trace+answer split into C-token chunks; learned = every non-final chunk also holds a full-state dump):

| C | full/tail N=8 | N=16 | N=32 | N=64 | learned k=4 N=64 | k=8 N=64 | k=16 N=32 | k=16 N=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 3 | 5 | 9 | 16 | 32 | 64 | None | None |
| 128 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 8 | 10 | 13 | 11 | 22 |
| 160 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 7 | 8 | 10 | 7 | 13 |
| 192 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 6 | 7 | 5 | 10 |
| 224 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 5 | 6 | 4 | 7 |
| 256 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 3 | 6 |

- **Chosen C = 192 (proposal: 256).** Rule: smallest C with (1) N=16 needs >= 2 chunks, (2) N=64 fits in <= 10 chunks in full/tail mode, (3) N=64 fits in <= 12 chunks in learned mode for every k when each chunk also carries a full-state dump.
- Why not 256: at ~14.5 tokens/line an N=16 trace (~250 tokens) fits in one 256-token chunk, so N=8 and N=16 would never cross a boundary and memory would not be exercised.
- Why not 128: a full k=16 dump costs ~78 tokens, leaving ~50 tokens (~3 trace lines) per learned chunk, so learned mode needs 22 chunks for N=64 and 11 for N=32 at k=16 (budget 12). C=160 still needs 13 at k=16, N=64.
- Side effect: tail m=200 >= C=192 means tail-200 keeps the entire previous chunk (still not full context).
- N=8 never crosses a chunk boundary at C=192 (it is a no-memory control cell).

## 5. Design decisions

- k is mixed within every run (k ~ U{4, 8, 16} per program); eval slices by k. No separate k sweep.
- Learned-mode truncation: the content of the LAST `<mem>` span of the chunk is cut to its FIRST m tokens (head kept). `pc` is always written first and registers in alphabetical order, so pc survives any m >= ~4. Tags are not counted toward m. Missing/unterminated/malformed span -> empty state.
- Learned mode ends a chunk at `</mem>` (MEM1-style: the model decides when to write memory and move on).
- Two warm-up checkpoints: `warmup_plain` (no `<mem>` at all) initializes full and tail runs; `warmup_mem` (same programs/traces + full-state dumps every U[lo, hi] steps, hi = lines that fit in one C-token chunk with a dump) initializes learned runs only. Training the tail model on dumps would pre-teach it to write state and confound tail vs learned (mentor's point).
- To tell tail and learned apart after RL, every boundary state is logged; state fidelity is computed for tail windows too (registers parsed from trace lines / any `<mem>` in the window vs. the true state at the referenced step).
- Full-context baseline is budget-matched: same C x max_chunks (192 x 12) generation budget, same warm-up recipe and the same number of GRPO steps. In full mode all previous outputs are kept after `Trace:` (exactly the SFT format).
- Oracle-state SFT is treated as a reference point, not an upper bound (it gets supervision RL never sees). Not run yet.
- Reward: 1 iff the final `Answer:` equals the true value; out of chunks = 0. Advantage normalized within each group of 8 and applied to every chunk of the rollout; groups with zero reward variance contribute no gradient and are skipped.
- GRPO: one optimizer step per GRPO step by default (ppo_epochs=1, num_minibatches=1), so pi_old = pi_theta and the clip is inactive; multiple minibatches/epochs and k3 KL to the warm-up adapter are implemented as flags.
- Prompt (SFT, env, eval): `Program:\n<program>\nState: <state>\nTrace:\n` (`State:` with nothing after it when empty). No chat template.
- Verbose trace lines (`1: c=c+a=12+07=19.`) keep per-step arithmetic trivial; terse format available via flag.
- Query register is one written in the last ceil(N/4) steps.

## 6. Changes from the proposal / things that broke

- C changed from 256 to 192 (see tokenization section).
- Run count: 14 RL runs (not 6 + 4). See run table.
- Measured s_min is 20/40/72 tokens for k=4/8/16 (proposal: ~25/45/85). For m=25 and k=4, the minimal state fits (20 <= 25); for k=8/16, m=25 is below s_min, so H2 predicts degradation there by construction.
- Neither warm-up checkpoint has ever seen a non-empty `State:` field (both are full-context traces, per plan). Resuming from a carried state is learned purely by RL. If learned-mode reward stays ~0 at small N in the first RL steps, the fallback is to add resumption examples to warmup_mem (prompt = program + true state at a random step, completion = rest of trace) - this would be a change to the plan.
- Eval reuses the same chunked env as RL (mode=full for the warm-up eval) so the warm-up numbers are directly comparable to RL numbers.
- Local dev machine has no CUDA GPU: all GPU numbers come from the vast.ai A100; CPU tests cover interpreter, env, metrics, SFT and the GRPO loop with the HF-generate backend.
